turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'm okay, I guess. A bit tired, but not in too much pain.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Maybe a 3 or 4. It's more like discomfort than sharp pain.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Alright, we can manage that with medication. Are you feeling nauseous or have vomited at all?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No nausea, thank goodness. I was worried about that after reading online.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. How's your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort in your chest?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Breathing is fine. I feel a bit stuffy from the tube, but it's getting better.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Do you remember anything from the operating room or waking up?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Not really. I remember going to sleep and then waking up here. No scary moments, though.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Since you have diabetes and high blood pressure, we’ll keep a close eye on your vitals and sugar levels.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Thanks, I appreciate that. I was a bit worried about how my conditions might affect recovery.
